clue.text: Times received by bachelor with a model mind

indicators.note: what is received is taken in, so the first word's letters go inside the group that follows

parts.note: standard abbreviation for bachelor
taken as written
to model is to sit for an artist
as in three by four: multiplied by

explanation.surface: A bachelor is joined at times by a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: The multiplication sign is read 'by', so 'Times' gives that little word. 'With a model' looks like a companion, but 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after a child, which is what 'mind' means as a verb.

clue.text: Oil company's importing gems and guns

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the company's letters take in the gems

parts.note: BP, the oil company, with its possessive S
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A petroleum firm brings in jewels and firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guns' looks like weapons in the surface; it is slang for well-developed arm muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns is gym slang for the arm muscles, chiefly the biceps.

clue.text: Bagging promotion, that was impressive self-confidence

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a sack, so the exclamation holds the promotion

parts.note: the cry 'bravo!' greets an impressive performance
an ad is a promotion, an advert

explanation.surface: Someone lands a promotion and shows real assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was impressive' is the cry of applause itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold show of self-confidence, often more swagger than substance.

clue.text: Son riding bike, maintaining grand airs

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the two outer parts hold the letter between them

parts.note: taken as written
a bike is a bicycle
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A boy on a bicycle putting on grand airs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the son riding the bike sits above it. 'Grand airs' reads as haughtiness; split, 'airs' is the definition, meaning tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A song cycle is a set of songs, or airs, composed to be performed as a sequence.

clue.text: Bikini perhaps missing top shows damage

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: Bikini is a Pacific atoll, 'perhaps' marking it as an example

explanation.surface: A topless two-piece swimsuit shows wear and tear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini Atoll, in the Marshall Islands, gave the swimsuit its name and was the site of US nuclear tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is the cost or damage something inflicts, as in 'take a toll'.

clue.text: After wine, friend makes a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: tells us the second element comes later, so the friend follows the wine

parts.note: rosé, the pink wine
American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: After a drink with a pal, somebody makes a small blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which is the surface reading; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is an unopened flower, literally part of a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Podgy king: he departed during tournament

parts.note: a podgy figure is round
R for rex, Latin for king
ob., short for obiit, Latin for 'he died'
in means during, as in 'in the night'

explanation.surface: A tubby monarch dies in the middle of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies its own synonym at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a tournament in which every competitor plays every other.

clue.text: Note service returning to this point

parts.note: so, or soh, the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so this word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Royal Air Force, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A message saying a service is coming back here.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is an idiom meaning up to now, to this point in time.

clue.text: Rind of Emmental in Russian food and drink

indicators.note: says those letters go inside the food word

parts.note: blini are small Russian pancakes

indicators.note: the rind is the outside of a cheese, so only the outer letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of Emmental

explanation.surface: A cheese rind tucked into a Russian meal with something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food and drink' sounds like a whole menu; 'drink' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bellini is a cocktail of prosecco and peach purée, invented at Harry's Bar in Venice.

clue.text: Reform urged: beg one to correct errors

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaigner pleads for someone to put mistakes right.
explanation.definitionFit: A debugger is a program, or a person, that finds and fixes errors in software.

clue.text: Fancy furs on new designer clothes move from side to side

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it
to clothe something is to wrap it up, so the designer's name goes around a letter

parts.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: as a verb of fancy dress, 'fancy' suggests letters dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Showy furs on a fashion designer's new collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is an old British word for a TV channel ('the other side' was ITV), so moving between sides is flicking channels.
explanation.definitionFit: To channel-surf is to hop restlessly between television channels with the remote.

clue.text: Fat reduced by female dog

indicators.note: something reduced by an amount has that amount taken away

parts.note: flab is body fat
standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Fat cut down, thanks to a bitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female dog' reads as one phrase, but 'female' belongs to the wordplay and 'dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lab is the everyday short form of Labrador, a breed of retriever dog.

clue.text: Caper in country whose leader is ousted by pressure

indicators.note: the first letter is thrown out and replaced by what follows

parts.note: a country in Europe
standard abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A scandal in a nation whose head is forced out under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' reads as an escapade or scandal, but it is the verb: to skip about.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper and to prance both mean to leap or dance about in a lively way.

clue.text: Reverential, installing last of garden decking

indicators.note: to install is to put inside, so the first word holds the letter

parts.note: adoring means worshipful or reverential

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the following word only

parts.note: the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: Someone devoutly fitting out the garden with decking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decking' looks like the wooden platform in the garden, but it is the verb: to deck is to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Decking a hall and adorning it both mean decorating it with ornaments.

clue.text: Awkwardly move vehicle around wood here

parts.note: to lumber is to move clumsily

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so read the vehicle backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart, as used by brewers

explanation.surface: Clumsily shifting a vehicle around the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberyard is a place where timber is stored and sold, so wood is found here.

clue.text: Excitedly, one came into banks over opening of fantastic account

indicators.note: banks line both sides of a river, so the jumble sits either side of a short word
something done excitedly is jumbled and agitated, so these letters get muddled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
as in 'time's up': finished

explanation.surface: Someone bursts excitedly into riverbanks just as a tall tale begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the anagram; 'over' is the short word the jumble wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional opening line of a fairy tale, a fantastic account.

clue.text: Stupidity of answer getting disdainful remark by head

parts.note: standard abbreviation for answer
'pish!' is an exclamation of contempt
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A daft reply earns a scornful comment from the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher, but it is a headland; place names such as Shoeburyness keep the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Apishness is silly, monkey-like behaviour, hence foolishness or stupidity.

clue.text: Pinch of salt roughly put in pies the wrong way

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor; AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: going the wrong way means backwards, so those pies are read in reverse
says the rough figure is placed inside the pies

parts.note: tarts are pies
c. for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A cookery note: sprinkle a little salt carelessly into pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch of salt' is a kitchen measure, but 'Pinch' stands alone as the definition: to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract can mean to take away or steal, so it is a formal synonym for pinch.

clue.text: Harry very bitter about a kind of animal abuse

parts.note: to harry someone is to pester or badger them

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bitter word goes around the single letter

parts.note: biting cold or wit is sharply bitter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Harry is very bitter about some form of cruelty to animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name, but it is a verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Badger-baiting, setting dogs on a captive badger, is an illegal blood sport and so a kind of animal cruelty.

clue.text: Severe health worker put on white coat after removing cereal

indicators.note: removing means taking letters out of the word just before

parts.note: Dr, a doctor
Asti is a white sparkling wine from Italy
taken as written
oats are a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A medic puts on a white coat after taking off the cereal stains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White coat' reads as a doctor's coat, but the words split: 'white' is a wine, and 'coat' loses OAT to leave C.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are severe, harsh or extreme ones.

clue.text: Gallons given to seaman in bars

parts.note: standard abbreviation for gallons
a rating is a non-officer sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor in a pub is handed gallons of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests pubs where a sailor drinks; it means a frame of metal bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating is a framework of parallel or crossed metal bars.

clue.text: Becoming crafty keeping tabs on Mike

indicators.note: to keep is to hold inside, so the crafty word holds the rest

parts.note: sly means cunning or crafty
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so two tabs
Mike is the radio code word for M

explanation.surface: A sly person secretly keeping watch on someone called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping tabs on' reads as one phrase meaning watching; split, 'tabs' is drugs slang for pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in the sense of suitable or attractive matches seemly, meaning proper or fitting.

clue.text: Who may work with horse shoes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who prepare racehorses

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a farrier shoeing horses; the shoes are in fact sports shoes, and the horse people are coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorse trainers condition horses for races, and trainers are also soft sports shoes.

clue.text: Not all charlatans raised from birth

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upward, so backwards
only part of the following word is used, so look inside it

parts.note: the letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Not every fraudster was brought up that way from birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, so here it stands for from birth.

clue.text: Melodic fragment wears thin for the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so we go by the sound of the words

parts.note: cloth that wears thin frays

explanation.surface: A tune's snippet gets tiresome for the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a phrase is a short unit of melody, a fragment of a longer tune.

clue.text: Make a copy of content-free, sardonic article

indicators.note: with its contents emptied out, only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of sardonic
an, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Copying out a sardonic piece with no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a newspaper piece; it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to make a digital copy of it with a scanner.

clue.text: Fitting edging for adult coats quietly

indicators.note: a coat goes around something, so those letters wrap another
the edging of a word is its border, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of adult
p, piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A grown-up's trim neatly put on someone's coat, without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and fitting are synonyms: both mean suitable for the occasion.

clue.text: Right doctrine confused i.e. Mrs Mop at first

indicators.note: says which piece is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: a mop or thatch of hair is a thick untidy head of it

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so they need sorting into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady muddles a right-wing creed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mop is a British name for a charwoman, which pulls 'Mrs Mop' together; split, 'Mop' means a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcherism is the political ideology of Margaret Thatcher, a right-wing doctrine.

clue.text: Got stuck into light food to start with

indicators.note: says the second piece comes at the beginning of the answer

parts.note: tack is food, as in hardtack ship's biscuit
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone tucked into a light snack as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light food' reads as one dish, but the two words are separate pieces, with the food placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: To get stuck into a job, in British idiom, is to tackle it with energy.

clue.text: Awfully curious borders for one area for flowers

indicators.note: a border runs around the edge, so the first word goes around the rest

parts.note: awfully curious, prying, is nosy
e.g., for example
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Peculiar edging for a single patch of flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' and 'flowers' paint a garden, but 'borders' is the verb: surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of flowers, a posy.
